result.title: Precedence-Aware Resource Allocation: Extending the AUTOC Framework to Multi-Level Treatments
result.summary: Many real-world decision problems require allocating limited resources across individuals to maximize total benefit often through interventions that vary in intensity rather than binary treat-or-not decisions. In these settings, higher levels treatments require first applying lower levels of treatment, inducing a precedence constraint that complicates allocation under a fixed budget. While the causal inference literature has largely emphasized accurate estimation of conditional average treatment effects (CATE), recent work has shown that estimation accuracy alone does not guarantee effective resource allocation, motivating ranking-based evaluation frameworks. The Area Under the Targeting Operating Characteristic (AUTOC) provides an effective way to evaluate prioritization rules across budget levels, but existing formulations are limited to binary treatments. We introduce Multi-Level AUTOC (ML-AUTOC), which is a generalization for AUTOC designed for multi-level treatment settings with precedence. We also propose precedence-aware policies for mapping true marginal treatment effects to feasible treatment assignments under fixed budget constraints. Our results show that in the setting of multi-level treatments, maximizing realized treatment effects may require re-allocation of treatments across individuals.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将用于预算分层评估优先排序规则的 AUTOC 框架推广到带前置约束的多级（非二元）干预场景，提出 ML-AUTOC 及将真实边际处理效应映射为固定预算下可行分配的前置感知策略，并指出最大化实际效应可能需要跨个体重新分配干预。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属因果推断与资源分配领域，其「固定预算下带前置约束的分层分配」与「按预算水平评估排序规则」的曲线式评价，可能为 LVR 中分阶段计算分配、THINK/LOOK/STOP 的预算-收益曲线评价提供问题表述与评估思路，可供核查。
